## 2B.2 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** I found **no credible 2024 evidence** that Marcos initiated or prolonged a war of choice, annexation, covert destabilization, or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity. The record instead shows repeated **de-escalation, formal incident-management, and refusal of offensive escalation** in the South China Sea. The main limiting evidence is a deterrence-heavy alliance posture, but that is not the same as offensive war expansion.

| ID | Direction | Title / Publisher / Date / URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | [PH, Viet Nam sign agreements on rice trade, agriculture, SCS incident prevention and management](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/) - Presidential Communications Office, 2024-01-30 | Marcos’s Vietnam visit produced a formal South China Sea **incident-prevention and management** agreement plus coast-guard cooperation. This is evidence of risk-reducing diplomacy, not war expansion. | `2B.2`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E2 | Favorable | [China, Philippines agree on 'provisional arrangement' for South China Sea resupply missions, Manila says](https://www.theprint.in/world/china-philippines-agree-on-provisional-arrangement-for-south-china-sea-resupply-missions-manila-says/2184146/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-07-21 | Manila and Beijing reached a provisional arrangement and framed it as a way to **de-escalate** and handle differences through dialogue. This is the strongest evidence against expansion of conflict beyond defensive necessity. | `2B.2`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| E3 | Favorable | [Marcos rejects use of water cannons to retaliate vs. Chinese vessels](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1224081) - Philippine News Agency, 2024-05-06 | Marcos said the Philippines would **not** use water cannons and had no intention of attacking with offensive measures. This is direct evidence against initiating cross-border coercion. | `2B.2`, `2B.1`, `1B.5`, `1B.3` |
| E4 | Favorable | [Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/) - Reuters / ThePrint, 2024-06-23 | Marcos said the Philippines was **not in the business of instigating wars** and would settle disputes peacefully, while refusing force or intimidation. This is broad anti-war-of-choice evidence from the ruler himself. | `2B.2`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.5` |
| E5 | Favorable / limiting | [Philippines says China's maritime-related proposals run contrary to its interests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippines-says-chinas-maritimerelated-proposals-run-contrary-to-its-interests-3333337) - Reuters, 2024-03-12 | Marcos did not reject Chinese proposals outright on militant grounds; he said the Philippines had difficulty with the premise and needed a path forward. This shows bargaining and resistance, but not annexation, proxy conflict, or offensive expansion. | `2B.2`, `2B.1`, `1B.4` |
| E6 | Limiting context | [Philippines, US to hold military drills in islands facing South China Sea, Taiwan](https://www.yahoo.com/news/philippines-us-hold-military-drills-074919409.html) - Reuters, 2024-03-05 | Balikatan 2024 moved toward sensitive islands and added cyber/information-warfare training. This is a deterrence-heavy posture, but it is still not evidence of wars of choice or covert destabilization beyond defense. | `2B.2`, `1B.3`, `1B.9` |
| E7 | Limiting context | [Philippines holds drills with allies after South China Sea confrontation](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/united-states-japan-philippine-conduct-maritime-exercises-in-south-china-sea-3758253) - Reuters, 2024-12-05 | Manila held maritime drills with the U.S. and Japan after another confrontation with Beijing. That shows continued alliance signaling and operational tempo, but still not offensive war expansion or proxy conflict. | `2B.2`, `1B.1`, `1B.8` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence against 2B.2:** Marcos repeatedly chose **incident-prevention agreements, provisional arrangements, and explicit non-offensive restraint** in 2024.
- **What is missing:** I found **no reliable evidence** of annexation, covert destabilization, proxy warfare, or an expanded war of choice.
- **Limiting context:** The Philippines did keep a **strong deterrence posture** with allied drills, which raises tension, but the record still points to **defensive necessity rather than offensive expansion**.

**Working judgment for 2B.2:** **No.** The 2024 record does **not** support the claim that Marcos initiated or expanded wars of choice or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity.
